notes: τά keeps the correlative such … as along with its nominal things: rule 31's carve-out gives the article the supplied relativizer where its modifier is a verbless prepositional phrase. Giving as to πρός instead remains defensible and the note records it.
πρός is unrepresented because the ASV absorbs it into the recast predicate we needed, which is the one case rule 36 allows a preposition to stand empty.
ἐπιτίθημι keeps both the preverb's on and the supplied board inside its own unit, headed on the verb word put (rule 106).
